priya:domicile-gate.headline: F-1 status blocks domicile in Virginia

reasoning_steps.claim: The student holds F-1 status, a temporary (student) visa.
Holders of student or temporary visas do not have the capacity to establish domicile in Virginia. No further domicile analysis is performed.

rule_citation.text: Holders of student or temporary visas do not have the capacity to establish domicile in Virginia.
rule_citation.authority: Part II, Section 03(A) & Section 02(4); SCHEV Domicile Guidelines, Code of Virginia 23.1-510(D)

finding.headline: Domicile clock started 8 Jun 2026 — the earliest in-state term begins 8 Jun 2027

reasoning_steps.claim: The student holds LPR status, which is not one of the statuses that close domicile in Virginia (F-1, J-1 and M-1). The gate does not fire, so the analysis continues — Part II, Section 03(A) & Section 02(4).

At the date of alleged entitlement the student is 22, under the pack's threshold of 24, so dependency is rebuttably presumed. It is rebutted: the "graduate or professional student" exception is established by the record itself. The timeline carries a masters-level program starting 24 Aug 2026 at School Z, on or before the date of alleged entitlement. The student's own acts are therefore what the intent analysis reads — Section 09(C)(1).

Of the 6 intent factors the guidelines weigh, 3 are satisfied and count: continuous residence (primary), drivers license (secondary) and VA job offer accepted (primary); 1 is satisfied but does not count: employment — "Co-op employment confers no domicile."; 1 cannot apply to this student: voter registration (immigration.status != 'citizen'); 1 is not on the record: VA income tax filed (primary) — SCHEV Domicile Guidelines, Code of Virginia 23.1-510(D).

1 of the qualifying factors is named in the pack's auxiliary-acts warning — drivers license (secondary). "Acts auxiliary to educational objectives, or routinely performed by temporary residents, carry little weight." They support the case; they do not carry it. — Section 06(B).

The last qualifying factor is VA job offer accepted on 8 Jun 2026, and the clock starts there. The clock does NOT start on arrival; look at the date on which the LAST of the qualifying factors occurred. Counting from the earliest factor instead (continuous residence, 1 Aug 2024) is the mistake this rule exists to prevent. — Section 05(C)(1).

365 days from 8 Jun 2026 is 8 Jun 2027 — the earliest date of alleged entitlement that satisfies the duration requirement. The date claimed here is 24 Aug 2026 (first official day of class of the term), which falls 288 days short.

In complex cases, construe the facts in the light most favorable to the student. This record is not a simple one: 1 satisfied factor that a pack caveat takes back out, 1 factor that cannot apply to this status, 1 earlier immigration status on the record and 1 open question. Every reading above that could go either way has gone the student's way, and the officer is directed to do the same. — SCHEV guidance

A prior determination by one institution is not binding on another. The record spans 2 institutions. A domicile determination made by one of them — favourable or not — does not bind the next, so this analysis has to be made again wherever the student is claiming in-state status.

No student shall be denied in-state tuition solely because of parental status. The age presumption applied and was rebutted by the graduate or professional student exception — so the student's own acts are what is weighed, and their parents' domicile is not by itself a reason to deny in-state status.

priya:aid-eligibility.headline: F-1 status blocks Virginia state financial aid

reasoning_steps.claim: F-1 status blocks Virginia state financial aid. Virginia state aid is closed by that one fact, before any question of need, merit or paperwork is reached.

F-1 status blocks Virginia state financial aid, and that block sits inside the form-selection rule itself — so the FAFSA route is closed too. The state alternative is only for students who cannot file the FAFSA, but it applies for the very aid this status blocks, so filing it would not reopen the door. What remains is institutional and private aid, which the financial aid office administers directly.
Domicile provision — Qualifies via VA domicile (see va-domicile pack). none of its one required item on record yet; still missing: Domicile established.
Tuition equity provision — Qualifies under tuition-equity provision. 1 of 3 required items on record: Tax filing evidence; still missing: VA high school attendance, VA high school graduation.
The deadline that binds is 1 Feb 2027 (college priority date) — the earliest of the three, ahead of state deadline 1 Mar 2027, federal deadline 30 Jun 2027. 192 days of margin from today.
Campuses are legally prohibited from sharing VASA application information for immigration enforcement. Underpins the no-account / no-store privacy posture.

rule_citation.text: Students eligible for FAFSA should file FAFSA (covers both federal and state aid). VASA is for students who cannot file FAFSA (e.g., undocumented / tuition-equity students).
rule_citation.authority: SCHEV VASA guidance; Federal Student Aid (FAFSA)

priya:next-steps.title: Report a qualifying job before your unemployment cap runs out
priya:next-steps.why: 70 of 90 unemployment days are already spent, and the count is cumulative — every day of the gap counts, not just the longest one. The STEM extension is not adding days, because no qualifying employment is on record yet.
priya:next-steps.leadTimeReason: SEVIS reporting has its own 10-day window, and a job that starts on the final day leaves no room to report it — the job has to start, and be reported, before the cap.
priya:next-steps.consequenceOfMissing: If the gap continues, SEVIS auto-terminates the F-1 record on 14 Aug 2026. There is no grace period and no reinstatement.

priya:next-steps.title: Confirm your CPT total with your DSO
priya:next-steps.why: PathWise counts 342 full-time CPT days at the master's level, and 54 of them exist only because 2 part-time authorizations overlapped into a full-time day — 23 short of the 365-day cliff.
priya:next-steps.leadTimeReason: This has to be settled BEFORE the next authorization is signed, not after — and a DSO appointment is not same-day.
priya:next-steps.consequenceOfMissing: 365 or more days of full-time CPT removes OPT eligibility entirely. Usage runs on authorized periods, not hours actually worked. Overtime and unemployment are not recomputed. A single authorization signed without checking the total can cross the cliff on paper alone.

priya:next-steps.title: Decide what follows your OPT before the authorization ends
priya:next-steps.why: Work authorization at the master's level runs to 15 Feb 2027, and all 12 months at this level are committed — there is nothing left to extend.
priya:next-steps.deadlineLabel: last day of work authorization at this level
priya:next-steps.leadTimeReason: The filing window for practical training opens 90 days ahead — treat that as the runway for arranging whatever comes next, too.
priya:next-steps.consequenceOfMissing: After 15 Feb 2027 the only cushion is the 60-day grace period, and it requires a qualifying action taken BEFORE the authorization expires — not after.

priya:next-steps.leadTimeReason: Aid offices ask for supporting documents after they read the form, and that request has to fit inside the window too.
priya:next-steps.consequenceOfMissing: Miss 1 Feb 2027 and the aid that date controls is allocated without this student — the federal deadline on 30 Jun 2027 is 149 days later and does not rescue it.
